headline: Town boards prepared for October Special Town Meeting amidst sharp divisions over CPA funding, while Neary School renovation options were narrowed.
synopsis: In September, Southborough boards focused on the October 17 Special Town Meeting warrant, elementary school facilities, and commercial development along Route 9. Town committees split sharply on capital spending, with the Advisory Committee voting against Community Preservation Act appropriations for golf course irrigation and a pedestrian trail bridge, as well as a proposed two-family zoning amendment. The Elementary School Building Committee narrowed its plans for Neary School after reviewing preliminary estimates ranging from $24.4 million to $49.2 million, eliminating an exterior addition and focusing on interior renovations. On Route 9, the Planning Board opened public hearings on a proposal by Costco Wholesale to build a 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 30-pump fueling station. Meanwhile, municipal departments drafted fiscal year 2028 operating budgets under competing scenarios, preparing for deep service reductions if a planned tax override question fails.

top_items.title: Neary School Building Committee eliminates Option 4, focuses on renovations
top_items.why: Preliminary cost estimates for Neary Elementary School renovation and addition options ranged from $24.4 million to $49.2 million. The committee voted 3-1 to eliminate Option 4 and directed architects to focus on interior options and a $15 million baseline.
top_items.body: Facing estimated costs well above the $15 million figure previously cited to voters, the Elementary School Building Committee voted to eliminate Option 4, an exterior gymnasium addition that encountered poor soils and high groundwater. Consultants were directed by a 4-0 vote to focus on Option 1 (code compliance and repairs), Option 3 (renovations with an enclosed courtyard gymnasium), and an analysis detailing what scope can be achieved for a $15 million baseline.

top_items.title: Planning Board opens hearing on proposed Coslin Drive Costco
top_items.why: Costco Wholesale presented initial site and traffic plans for a 167,000-square-foot retail warehouse and 30-position gas station spanning 26.12 acres on the Westborough town line. Board members and residents raised concerns regarding traffic congestion along Route 9 and surrounding neighborhood streets.
top_items.body: Costco Wholesale submitted major site plan and special permit applications for a 167,000-square-foot store and a 30-position fueling station at 21 Coslin Drive. During the initial hearing, Southborough residents expressed concerns about traffic impacts along Route 9, truck turnarounds at Route 85, and cut-through traffic on Flagg Road. The Planning Board continued the public hearing to October 19.

top_items.title: Town boards clash over CPA funding for golf irrigation
top_items.why: The Select Board and Community Preservation Committee endorsed appropriating over $433,000 in Community Preservation Act funds for a new Southborough Golf Club irrigation system. The Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against recommending the article for Special Town Meeting.
top_items.body: After bids exceeded previous town appropriations, the total estimated cost to replace the Southborough Golf Club irrigation system rose to nearly $1.09 million. The proposal calls for $100,000 from the golf course revolving fund and $433,346 in additional CPA money. While the Select Board supported the article, Advisory Committee members argued against using tax-backed CPA funds for a municipal golf course intended to be self-sustaining.

top_items.title: Peninsula Trail footbridge faces resistance ahead of Town Meeting
top_items.why: The Trails Committee and Community Preservation Committee advanced an article requesting $217,318 in supplemental CPA funds for a 65-foot prefabricated pedestrian bridge. Both the Select Board (1-4) and the Advisory Committee (0-7) voted against supporting the appropriation.
top_items.body: The Trails Committee sought additional CPA funds to cover cost escalations for a pedestrian bridge connecting sections of the Peninsula Trail along Route 30, bringing the total estimated project cost to $428,550. Opponents on the Select Board and Advisory Committee cited high costs and broader municipal budget pressures, prompting trail advocates to prepare public outreach and a potential warrant amendment extending existing funds.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee opposes two-family zoning code amendment
top_items.why: An amendment proposed by the Zoning Board of Appeals would eliminate the two-year waiting period to convert single-family homes into two-family dwellings. The Advisory Committee voted 3-4 against recommending the article, while the Select Board and ZBA endorsed it.
top_items.body: Article 2 on the Special Town Meeting warrant seeks to clarify zoning definitions and remove the requirement that a single-family home exist for two years before converting to two-family housing. Advisory Committee opponents voiced concerns about residential density, school impacts, and septic capacity, while proponents pointed to regional housing shortages and expanded options. The Planning Board continued its hearing on the proposal to October 17.

top_items.title: Departments model service cuts under FY28 budget guidelines
top_items.why: Department heads were directed to submit two FY28 budget scenarios, including a zero-percent increase option anticipating the potential failure of a spring tax override. The Personnel Board voted to recommend a 5% total salary adjustment.
top_items.body: Ahead of a planned spring tax override ballot question, Southborough departments prepared two fiscal year 2028 budgets. While Request A maintains level services with a recommended 3% cost-of-living adjustment and 2% step increment, Request B holds spending to fiscal year 2027 levels. Library, Health, and Conservation officials reported that flat funding would force staff hour reductions and eliminate operational and program line items.

top_items.title: Select Board appoints interim clerk and advances appointed role
top_items.why: The Select Board voted unanimously to appoint Amy Berry as interim town clerk through May 2027 following the departure of Jim Hegarty. Article 1 on the Special Town Meeting warrant proposes making the town clerk an appointed position.
top_items.body: Amy Berry, previously a Southborough deputy town clerk and current Grafton town clerk, was appointed to serve as interim town clerk from October 1 through May 11, 2027. Both the Select Board and Advisory Committee voted to recommend approval of Special Town Meeting Article 1, which initiates changing the town clerk from an elected office to an appointed position subject to voter confirmation at the 2027 annual town election.

top_items.title: Select Board renews regional waste consortium participation
top_items.why: The Select Board voted unanimously to remain in a 35-town consortium negotiating bulk refuse disposal with WIN Waste. The town's existing waste agreement runs through December 31, 2027.
top_items.body: Department of Public Works Director Bill Cundiff briefed the Select Board on upcoming contract negotiations for municipal waste disposal at the WIN Waste facility in Millbury. Southborough has participated in the 35-community group led by Walpole since 2006. The board agreed that the pricing leverage of regional volume outweighs legal representation concerns and voted to remain in the collaborative.
